abstract: A novel therapy for improving selectivity in cancer chemotherapy aims to modify distribution of a cytotoxic drug by generating it selectively at tumour sites. In this approach an antibody-enzyme conjugate is allowed to localise at the tumour sites before injecting a prodrug which is converted to an active drug specifically by the targeted enzyme in the conjugate. We present here pharmacokinetic studies on the prodrug 4-(bis (2-chloroethyl) amino) benzoyl-L-glutamic acid and its activated derivative, benzoic acid mustard. The glutamic acid is cleaved from the prodrug to form the active drug by carboxypeptidase G2 (CPG2), an enzyme from Pseudomonas sp., which is not found in mammalian cells. The prodrug and its parent active drug were rapidly distributed in plasma and tissues after administration of prodrug or active drug (41 mumol kg-1 intraperitoneally) to mice bearing human choriocarcinoma xenografts. Prodrug and active drug both followed a two-compartment kinetic model. Prodrug was eliminated more rapidly (t1/2 alpha = 0.12 h, t1/2 beta = 0.70 h) than active drug (t1/2 alpha = 0.37 h, t1/2 beta = 1.61 h). Conversion of the prodrug to the activated parent drug was detected within 5 min of administration to mice which had previously received a F(ab')2-anti-human chorionic gonadotrophin antibody (W14A) conjugated to the enzyme, CPG2 (1,000 U kg-1). Tumour was the only tissue that activated all the prodrug reaching the site. It contained the highest concentration of targeted enzyme conjugate capable of catalysing the reaction of prodrug to drug. Plasma and other tissues were also capable of activating the prodrug but active drug production was limited by the amount of enzyme present. The active drug measured in plasma and tissues other than tumour was attributable to residual antibody-enzyme conjugate at non-tumour sites. Low levels of conjugate in tissues and plasma militate against the advantage of tumour localised enzyme therefore necessitating removal of non-localised enzyme.
abstract_ja: 治療効果を高める新たな方法として、腫瘍部位で細胞傷害性薬剤を選択的に生成させる手法がある。本アプローチでは、抗体-酵素結合体を腫瘍部位に集積させたうえで、結合した酵素によって特異的に活性型へ変換されるプロドラッグを投与する。本論文では、プロドラッグ4-(ビス(2-クロロエチル)アミノ)ベンゾイル-L-グルタミン酸およびその活性化誘導体である安息香酸マスタードの薬物動態を検討した。マウスにヒト絨毛癌異種移植片を担がんさせ、プロドラッグまたは活性薬物（41 μmol/kg、腹腔内投与）を投与した。両者とも二区画モデルに従った。プロドラッグの消失は活性薬物より速かった（t1/2α = 0.12 h, t1/2β = 0.70 h、活性薬物はそれぞれ0.37 h, 1.61 h）。F(ab')2-抗ヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン抗体（W14A）に結合させた酵素CPG2（1,000 U/kg）を事前投与したマウスでは、投与後5分以内にプロドラッグから活性体への変換が確認された。腫瘍は、そこに到達したプロドラッグのすべてを活性化する唯一の組織であった。腫瘍には標的酵素結合体が最も高濃度に存在し、プロドラッグから薬物への反応を触媒することができた。血漿および腫瘍以外の組織もプロドラッグを活性化できたが、活性薬物の産生は存在する酵素量に制限された。腫瘍以外の組織や血漿中で測定された活性薬物は、非腫瘍部位に残存する抗体-酵素結合体に起因した。組織や血漿中の結合体濃度が低いことは、腫瘍局在型酵素の利点を損なうため、非局在化酵素の除去が必要であることを示している。
